lesson.grammar_point: superlative adjectives (the -est / the most / the best / the worst)

listenings.text: Good afternoon, everybody. It is time for the awards of the year. This year was not easy, but our results are the best in five years. The award for the most efficient plant goes to France. The award for the best delivery goes to Brazil: ninety-eight percent on time, the highest number in the group. Congratulations, Rodrigo, and congratulations to the team in Brazil! And a special award, for the most improved team, goes to Shanghai. Thank you all, and let us make next year even better.

New York in numbers. The tallest building in the city is One World Trade Center, one thousand seven hundred and seventy-six feet. The biggest park is not Central Park. It is Pelham Bay Park, in the Bronx. The busiest subway station is Times Square, with more than fifty million people a year. And the oldest bridge in the city? It is not the Brooklyn Bridge. It is the High Bridge, from eighteen forty-eight.

extra_audio.text: Claire opened the forum with the ranking of the year. France was the biggest and the most efficient plant. Brazil had the fastest deliveries and got the award. Rodrigo said that transport was their worst result. At the end he presented the goal for next year: zero accidents.

reading.rtitle: Global Operations -- Plant Ranking of the Year
paras: Every year the group compares its plants in five results: safety, cost, delivery, quality and energy. Here is the ranking for this year.
1. FRANCE. The biggest plant in the group, and this year the most efficient. It had the lowest cost per kilo and zero safety problems.
2. BRAZIL. The fastest deliveries in the group: ninety-eight percent on time. Brazil also had the best result in quality.
3. UNITED STATES. The most modern plant in the group, but the cost of energy was the highest.
4. CHINA. The newest plant. It had the worst year in delivery, but its team is the youngest, and it is growing fast.
The award for the best delivery goes to Brazil. The goal for next year is the same for every plant: zero accidents.
